newsitem.title: USA: NCAA BASKETBALL-DEAN SMITH SURPASSES RUPP'S WINS RECORD.
newsitem.headline: NCAA BASKETBALL-DEAN SMITH SURPASSES RUPP'S WINS RECORD.

text.p: Dean Smith knew it would come sooner or later, but it was just a little sweeter that it came now: win number 877.

Smith broke the Division I wins record of legendary Kentucky coach Adolph Rupp when top-seeded North Carolina rolled to a 73-56 victory over ninth-seeded Colorado in the second round of the NCAA Tournament East Region on Saturday.
Ed Cota scored a career-high 16 points and Antawn Jamison added 19 points and 16 rebounds for North Carolina (26-6), which has won 14 consecutive games.

"The nice thing is that nobody expected this year would be the time," said Smith, remembering that at one point this season, the Tar Heels were 9-4 overall and 0-3 in the Atlantic Coast Conference. "These players have accomplished a lot this year."

Smith, in his 36th season at North Carolina, steered the Tar Heels to their 21st regional semifinal under him and will play California in the East Region semifinals on Friday at the Carrier Dome in Syracuse, New York.
"Fortunately, I still have a job at the University of North Carolina," Smith said. "I never let people know it, but I have had several pro situations, beginning in 1970 and as late as a year ago.
"I talked to UCLA on two occasions, and that's about the closest I've come (to leaving). I'm one of the luckiest guys in the world to be at Chapel Hill and be a coach there."

In the final minute, with many of his former players in attendance, including current Sonics coach George Karl and forward Sam Perkins, the pro-North Carolina crowd began a chant of "Dean! Dean! Dean!"
"It's everybody at Carolina's so-called record," said Smith, sharing the credit with all the players who were a part of his run to the record. "One group of kids recuits another."
Fifth-seeded California advanced to the Sweet 16 when Tony Gonzalez scored a season-high 23 points in a 75-68 victory over fourth-seeded Villanova.
The Golden Bears (23-8) will be in the Sweet 16 for the first time since 1993, when they upset Duke in the second round.

In the Southeast Region in Memphis, Tennessee, Miles Simon scored 20 points and Mike Bibby hit two key free throws with 2.3 seconds left as fourth-seeded Arizona escaped with a 73-69 victory over 12th-seeded College of Charleston.
Bibby finished with 18 points for the Wildcats (21-9), who will play top-seeded Kansas in the Southeast Region semifinals at Birmingham, Alabama, on Friday.

Arizona had never won an NCAA Tournament game outside the West Region prior to this year. The Wildcats will be looking for payback from last year's West Region semifinals, when Kansas beat them 83-80.

"I think we're all just sick and tired of the negatives that some of you seem to have as the thing that you do," said Arizona coach Lute Olson, whose teams have been eliminated in the first round on three separate occasions since 1992 despite being seeded no lower than fifth.
Stacy Harris scored 25 points for College of Charleston (29-3), which had its 23-game winning streak snapped.
Kansas advanced to its fifth consecutive Sweet 16 as Paul Pierce had 20 points in a 75-61 victory over eighth-seeded Purdue.

In the West Region at Salt Lake City, Utah, Wayne Turner drive the lane three times for key baskets and Scott Padgett knocked down a 12-footer with 28 seconds to play as top-seeded and defending champion Kentucky turned back eighth-seeded Iowa 75-69.

Jared Prickett scored 15 points and Turner finished with 13 for Kentucky (32-4), which will play St. Joseph's in the regional semifinals Thursday at San Jose, California. The Wildcats have won eight straight NCAA Tournament games since a 74-61 loss to North Carolina in the 1995 East Region final.

Andre Woolridge scored 29 points and Ryan Bowen added 14 for Iowa (22-10), which has lost in the second round in its last six NCAA Tournament appearances. The Hawkeyes have not made the Sweet 16 since 1988.

Fourth-seeded St. Joseph's battled to an 81-77 overtime victory over fifth-seeded Boston College as Rashid Bey scored 10 of his 23 points in the extra session. St. Joseph's (26-6) reached the Sweet 16 for the first time since 1981.
In the Midwest at Auburn Hills, Michigan, Charles O'Bannon scored 28 points as second-seeded UCLA overcame an early deficit and cruised to a 96-83 victory over seventh-seeded Xavier.
The Bruins (23-7) play Iowa State in the Sweet 16 on Thursday.
Klay Edwards' layup with 30 seconds remaining was the difference as sixth-seeded Iowa State edged third seed Cincinnati 67-66.
Kenny Pratt scored 21 points and Dedric Willoughby had 19 for Iowa State (22-8), which advanced to its first regional semifinal since 1986.
